subject: Usage Insights beta: terminology (route vs endpoint) + docs framing
body:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Usage Insights beta: terminology (route vs endpoint) + docs framing

Hey Dylan — quick DevEx note after looking at the latest console copy for the Usage Insights beta.

We’re using “route” pretty heavily (e.g., “Cost by route + model”). I’m worried this will read as “my app routes” to a lot of folks, or feel like an internal infra term.

A few suggestions to reduce confusion:
- Prefer “API endpoint” in most user-facing places (tables, filters, headers).
- When we need precision, use “Endpoint (normalized)” or “Endpoint template” and show an example in the tooltip:
  - /v1/chat/completions
  - /v1/files/:file_id (example of templated path param)
- Reserve “route” for backend docs/ADR (“route normalization”) and maybe in parentheses.

Also: “Route” gets extra confusing for OpenAI-compat customers who think in “operation” names, not paths.

Can we align on a glossary term and update UI + docs? Happy to draft tooltip copy / a short definitions section.

– Alex
Alex Martinez
Developer Experience Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta: terminology (route vs endpoint) + docs framing

Agree with the concern.

Internally we’ve been saying “route” because the dimension is literally the normalized gateway route template (post-templating), and we’re trying to distinguish from “URL” (since query params are dropped, host varies, etc.).

But for the console, “API endpoint” is probably the least surprising.

Two edge cases we should be explicit about somewhere:
1) We normalize dynamic segments, so customers may not see the *exact* request path they sent.
2) We also bucket some OpenAI-compat endpoints to the canonical Redwood equivalents.

If you can propose final user-facing strings + tooltip content, I can feed it to the design ticket / copy pass.

-Dylan


From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 10:36 AM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta: terminology (route vs endpoint) + docs framing

Perfect. Here’s a first pass on the language.

Console UI (recommended):
- Page title: “Usage insights”
- Primary table header: “Cost by API endpoint and model”
- Filter label: “API endpoint”
- Column label: “Endpoint”

Tooltip copy for “API endpoint” filter/column:
“Endpoints are shown as normalized templates (e.g., /v1/files/:file_id). We group dynamic IDs into placeholders to keep reports stable and prevent high-cardinality breakdowns.”

Tooltip copy for “Why doesn’t this match my exact URL?” (maybe inline help):
“We remove query parameters and normalize dynamic path segments. If you use OpenAI-compatible endpoints, we may map them to canonical endpoints for reporting.”

Docs framing (help center):
- Short “Definitions” box near the top:
  - “Endpoint (normalized): The API path template used for aggregation.”
  - “Model (family/version): Stable model identifier used for reporting (aliases may be grouped).”

One more wording nit: “route + model” reads like a join key; “endpoint and model” reads more like what users expect.

If this makes sense, I can turn it into a short doc PR for Elliot/Wei later, but at minimum we should get tooltips + table headers aligned.

– Alex


From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 11:21 AM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta: terminology (route vs endpoint) + docs framing

This is good.

One nuance: we should avoid promising that OpenAI-compat endpoints “map” in all cases. Right now the normalization library does a mix of:
- templating dynamic segments
- canonicalizing some known compat paths
- fallback to “unknown/untemplated” if we can’t safely normalize

Could we tweak the compat sentence to something like:
“Some OpenAI-compatible paths may be grouped under a canonical endpoint for reporting.”

Also, I’ll add a note to ENG-3813 that user-facing terminology should be “endpoint” even if the internal field is route_template.


From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 1:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta: terminology (route vs endpoint) + docs framing

Yep — updated phrasing:

Revised tooltip line:
“If you use OpenAI-compatible paths, some requests may be grouped under a canonical endpoint for reporting.”

Also proposing one more UI copy tweak based on prior customer confusion (esp. finance folks):
- Instead of “Endpoint (normalized)” in the column header (which might look scary), keep it simple as “Endpoint”, but have the tooltip include “normalized template”.

If it helps design, here’s a compact tooltip version that fits:
“Endpoint is a normalized path template (e.g., /v1/files/:file_id). IDs are replaced with placeholders to keep reports stable and reduce cardinality.”

Let me know where you want this to land (design ticket vs PRD comments). I can paste into DES-912 notes if you already have that thread.

– Alex


From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 4:27 PM PST
Subject: Re: Usage Insights beta: terminology (route vs endpoint) + docs framing

Sounds good.

Action items on my side:
- Update console copy from “route” -> “API endpoint” (headers + filters) in the next UI pass.
- Add your tooltip text to the UX spec notes (I’ll drop into the design ticket + ping Tessa/Alicia in Slack).
- Add a short “Definitions” block request to the docs PR (Elliot/Wei) so it doesn’t get lost.

If you have time, please also add a quick comment to PM-1427 so Product sees the terminology decision and we don’t regress back to “route” in release notes.

Thanks for catching this before beta.

-Dylan
